chunks: Ali ibn Mahziyar from Fadalah ibn Ayyub from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdillah from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

"When you pray while facing away from the Qibla, and it becomes clear to you that you prayed while facing away from the Qibla, and you are within the time [of that prayer], then repeat [the prayer]; and if the time has passed for you, then do not repeat."

key_terms.الْقِبْلَةِ: The direction of prayer (towards the Kaaba in Mecca)
key_terms.فَأَعِدْ: Then repeat (imperative to perform the prayer again)
key_terms.فَاتَكَ الْوَقْتُ: The time has passed for you

ai.seo_question: Do I need to repeat my prayer if I realize I faced the wrong direction after the prayer time has passed?
ai.summary: This narration from Al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the temporal condition for re-performing Salah when the Qibla is incorrect, distinguishing between error during the prayer window versus after its expiration. It reflects the Shia juristic principle that the validity of the prayer is tied to the specific time slot, offering practical guidance for worshippers who discover directional errors post-prayer. The ruling emphasizes ease and avoids unnecessary burden by exempting those who realize the mistake only after the time has passed.
